title: Rerank evaluation harness: NDCG & MRR tracking with customer prompt sets and A/B experiment hooks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a production-grade evaluation harness for reranking endpoints that consistently tracks NDCG and MRR across customer prompt sets, supports per-request A/B labeling, and scales without adding tail latency to serving. This ticket delivers ingestion, storage schema, sliceable dashboards, and a small SDK to emit evaluation signals from frontend/backend callers. Goal is to make rerank quality regressions visible in CI and in production monitoring and to enable controlled online experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline computes NDCG@1/3/5 and MRR daily for each active customer prompt set and model variant
Per-query rerank logs (query text hashed, candidate ids, scores, chosen rank, ground-truth label if provided) persisted in S3 with partitioning by date and customer
A/B experiment tags accepted in the rerank API (header + request metadata) and propagated to eval logs
Dashboards show historical NDCG/MRR trends, by-customer and aggregated, with ability to filter by model version and experiment bucket
Compute pipeline completes within the daily window (<= 2 hours for 10M logged queries), and storage cost estimate validated
End-to-end test verifying metric calculation against synthetic dataset is present in the CI pipeline
technical_notes: Metric definitions: NDCG@k using graded relevance when ground-truth relevance provided; fallback to click proxy (binary) when not available; MRR computed with 1-based indexing
Logging design: synchronous small payloads (headers + meta) to avoid impacting token path; bulk async batch upload to S3 via a dedicated uploader service to avoid per-request S3 dependency
Storage: parquet files partitioned by date/customer/model_version; schema includes hashed_query, candidates[], scores[], chosen_index, label_type (gt/click), experiment_tag
Privacy: store hashed_query (SHA256) and customer id only; raw queries retained only for opt-in customers and separated behind restricted buckets
Scaling: uploader uses Kinesis-style shards with backpressure; compute pipeline is Spark job with incremental checkpoints; expect 2-3x compression vs JSON using parquet/snappy
Latency tradeoffs: synchronous path adds <1ms median overhead due to header parsing; where p99 impact >5ms, use sampling (1%) and route full logging via sampling flag
A/B hooks: API accepts X-Rerank-Experiment header + client-generated uuid; evaluation pipeline joins experiment buckets and surfaces per-bucket metrics with confidence intervals
Retention and cost: default 90-day hot retention for metrics, 1-year cold archives for raw logs; provide toggle per-customer
